What moved this estimate

Each factor's effect on the model's risk score, compared with the average record. Pink raises estimated risk; blue lowers it.

How to read this

  • The curve is the share of similar records the model expects to be recorded alive at each month. It is not a personal prognosis.
  • The band shows how much the estimate moves when the model is retrained on resampled data. Wider means less certain.
  • Factor bars explain the model, not biology. They describe associations in this dataset, not causes.
  • The model was tested on 1,207 held-out records from the same dataset only. It has not been validated anywhere else.
These are US SEER registry patients diagnosed 2006–2010, not Ghanaian women, and Status does not record cause of death. Do not use these estimates to inform anyone's care.

One decision tree from the forest

Grown on the 2,816 training records. Each box asks one question; each leaf shows the share of women recorded alive at 5 years.

Profile A

Swipe sideways to see the whole tree →

Yes goes left, no goes right. Tap any box to trace its path. Darker leaves had worse survival. Kaplan–Meier estimates from training data; research use only.

Why a forest?

One tree is easy to read but rough. The random survival forest grows 400 trees on resampled data and averages them.
